Sediment Transport module now catalogued using the dedicated 1D Sediment Transport User's Manual (1DSED-6.4.1) and 2D Sediment User's Manual (2DSED-6.4.1), both v6.4.1. Coverage: 1D - Quasi-Unsteady Flow Data and boundary conditions specific to sediment modeling (Flow Series, downstream Stage/Rating Curve/Normal Depth, lateral/uniform-lateral flow, T.S. Gate Openings, Internal Stage BC, quasi-unsteady and unsteady temperature series); Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters (transport function, sorting method, fall velocity method, Max Depth/Min Elevation, Movable Bed Limits, Multiple Movable Bed Limits, bed gradation template assignment); Bed Gradation Templates (incl. sample-specific cohesive parameters); full Sediment Boundary Conditions (rating curve incl. concentration mode and diversion load, manual and DSS load series, equilibrium load, clear water, junction/flow-split methods); Sediment Properties Options in full (grain class definitions, cohesive options incl. Kd/M thresholds, Bed Change Options incl. the global 2x2 channel/overbank erosion/deposition matrix, Reservoir/Distance-Decay/Rouse-Diffusion deposition methods, Simplified CEM erosion method, local XS overrides, area-volume conversion method; transport routing method and full transport-function calibration incl. scaling factors and direct parameter overrides; Lateral Structure diversion threshold and flow optimization; Bed Mixing Options incl. active layer thickness/min thickness/shape factor; Subsidence; classic and Pool Pass Through Nodes; Observed Profile Data); the full USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (cross-section configuration stations, groundwater elevation/mode, bank material selection and the full material parameter database incl. soil-strength, erodibility, and optional groundwater routing parameters, multi-layer bank definitions, and all BSTEM Options); Plan-level Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (bed exchange iterations, hydraulic/XS update thresholds, volume change method, transport energy slope method, bed roughness predictor and averaging reaches, computation run-time multiplier, cross-section weighting factors) and Simulation Time Window; the full Dredging Events editor (elevation and mass methods, set range of values, load re-introduction); Sediment Output Options and Tolerances in full (output level, mass/volume, output increment, XS bed change output, customized output variable selection, HDF5 toggle, current and legacy hotstart mechanisms, classic/legacy binary output toggles, DSS output); and the SIAM (Sediment Impact Analysis Methods) hydraulic-design tool in full (sediment reach definition, bed material, hydrology, sediment properties, sediment sources and their per-reach assignment, and all Options incl. user-defined particle sizes, XS exclusion, and budget tolerances). 2D (module=Sediment Transport, id prefix sed.2d.*, all sourced to 2DSED-6.4.1): 2D Bed Material Type association (Bed Gradation Template / Bed Layer Group / Non-erodible Surface), Bed Layer Groups, 2D Bed Gradation Templates; full 2D Sediment Boundary Conditions (rating curve, load series, equilibrium load, clear water, capacity ratio); 2D grain-class Density Method; 2D-only Cohesive Options (flocculation method incl. Hwang 1989 coefficients and user-specified flocculation curve, consolidation curve); the full Transport Methods/AD Parameters editor (total-load correction toggle, bed-load and suspended-load correction methods, diffusion coefficient method and value, adaptation-length method and value); 2D transport-function calibration (total-load scaling factor, mobility factor); the full 2D Options editor (Capacity Only Method, Sheet and Splash Erosion coefficient, Morphologic Acceleration Factor, Base Bed-Slope Coefficient, Hindered Settling, Avalanching); 2D-specific Bed Mixing Options (Hiding/Exposure Function, 2D active layer thickness method and minimum thickness); 2D sediment warmup periods; the full 2D Computational Options tab (subgrid erosion and deposition methods, advection scheme, matrix solver, outer-loop max iterations and convergence tolerances, computational sediment layer thickness parameters); and 2D Sediment Output Options (output level, output interval multiples, customized output variable selection, hotstart, restart). Excluded per scope (one-time transform/analysis actions, not persisted model data, consistent with the existing DSS-import exclusion precedent): the Histograph Generator (converts a flow file into a new equal-load-increment flow file), Create Geometry Files from Sediment Results, the Specific Gage Post-Processor, and the Cross Section Point Filter (already excluded under Geometry Editor). Excluded as pure output/results content (not input fields), matching the existing scope_note precedent for steady/unsteady output: the ~100+ selectable 1D and ~80 selectable 2D output-variable names themselves (represented instead as single consolidated 'customized output variable selection' entries per the task's guidance on output toggles that are actually input controls); the Sediment Results Viewer, Legacy Output, BSTEM Output tables, and all HDF5/log-file output schema documentation (Trouble Shooting, Viewing Results, Output Variables sections of both manuals). The 1D Sediment Transport Technical Reference Manual chapter (theory/derivations, no additional dialog fields beyond what the User's Manual chapter already exposes) and the Hydraulic Design Functions cross-referenced out to the main HEC-RAS User's Manual without inline field detail in these sediment manuals (Bridge Scour, Riprap and Scour Calculator, Uniform Flow, Stable Channel Design Tools, Sediment Transport Capacity Calculator, and the Sediment Rating Curve Analysis Tool) were NOT catalogued here - flagged rather than guessed, since primary-source field-level detail for these tools lives in UM-6.4.1/HRM-6.0, not in the sediment manuals, and they are general hydraulic-design tools rather than sediment-exclusive dialogs; a future pass sourcing UM-6.4.1 should confirm whether they belong under Sediment Transport, Structures, or a general Hydraulic Design Functions grouping. Flagged for live-HEC-RAS-7.0 confirmation rather than guessed: sed.2d.computation2d.max_subgrid_regions and sed.2d.computation2d.max_subgrid_length_scale (named and located only in the 2D manual's parameter-summary appendix, section 8 p.130, without prose-level control_type/valid_range detail in the main section 4.2 body text); whether the BSTEM Layer-Method-vs-Method-of-Slices choice (1DSED section 2.10.3, p.368) is ever user-selectable or purely automatic (the manual only describes it as an automatic fallback triggered by tension cracks/overhanging banks, so no field was added for it). Also noted but explicitly out of scope for this task (belongs to the already-catalogued 2D Flow Areas / Unsteady Flow Editor modules, not Sediment Transport): a 'Minimum Face Length Tolerance' mesh setting referenced in 2DSED-6.4.1 section 2.2.5 (p.26-27) as important for sediment mesh quality, and the 2D hydraulic Equation Set (Shallow Water vs Diffusion Wave) toggle referenced in 2DSED-6.4.1 section 2.4 (p.30-31) as consequential for sediment model credibility - both appear to be gaps in the existing 2D Flow Areas / Unsteady Flow Editor catalog entries, not sediment-specific fields, so they were not added under sed.* and are left for a future pass on those modules. Sediment Transport module is now considered fully catalogued against these two manuals. Remaining modules not yet catalogued: Water Quality, Plan/Run Manager, RAS Mapper. Both were added now as isolated, correctly-sourced entries (plan.comp_options.equation_set, mapper.options.min_face_length_tolerance) under their correct modules rather than left as an unfixed 2D Flow Areas gap or misfiled there. Remaining modules requiring a full dedicated Phase 0 pass: Water Quality, Plan/Run Manager, RAS Mapper. Water Quality module (module=Water Quality, id prefix wq.*) now catalogued using the dedicated Water Quality User's Manual (WQ-6.4.1, v6.4.1, obtained via a Wayback Machine save-on-demand capture triggered 2026-08-31 because direct fetch was blocked by the local network content filter and the capture was not yet indexed by archive.org's availability API at fetch time - see meta.sources for the full obtained_via note). Coverage: Physical Properties (wq.cell.* - default cell configuration and Minimum Water Quality Cell Length combining/Fixed Faces; wq.dispersion.* - user-assigned per-river-station dispersion coefficients and the model-computed-dispersion alternative with its multiplier and lower/upper limits); Meteorological Datasets (wq.met.* - dataset naming, physical location fields [reference elevation, lat/long, nearest standard meridian, non-georeferenced station x-y, picture filename], and the WQ-cell-to-dataset assignment method/table) and the six required weather time series (wq.weather.* - atmospheric pressure, air temperature, humidity [as RH/wet-bulb/dew-point/vapor pressure], cloudiness, solar radiation plus its dust coefficient, and wind speed plus anemometer-height correction and the TEMP-DLL wind-function calibration parameters a/b/c, diffusivity ratio Kh/Kw, and Use-Richardson-Number toggle); Boundary Conditions (wq.boundary.constituent_timeseries, consolidated across the shared four-source data-entry mechanism - Table Data/DSS/Excel Worksheet/Constant - used throughout this module); Initial Conditions (wq.initial.* - distribution table, restart-file-vs-distribution source selection, and restart file reference); Observed Data (wq.observed.* - time series, continuous-record-vs-grab-sample type, applicable display duration, and downstream-distance-from-gage spatial placement); the General Constituent Simulation Library / arbitrary constituents (wq.constituent.* - constituent count and naming, zero-order/first-order/sediment-release/settling parameters, temperature correction coefficient, and the instantaneous Mass Injection table); the Nutrient Simulation Library NSMII, Solar Radiation module selection, and Water Temperature (TEMP) DLL parameters (wq.library.* - active-library checklist across GCSM/NSMII/SOLIDS/TEMP/TEQ; NSMII per-state-variable Yes/No enable list and sediment-diagenesis option; the algal growth-limitation-function choice; and the five NSMII rate-constant/parameter tables for Algae, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, CBOD, and Dissolved Oxygen, each carrying manual-sourced QUAL2E suggested ranges, defaults, and temperature-correction coefficients per Tables 19-1 through 19-5; the EPA/KLEIN/MBH solar radiation module selection and each module's calibration parameters; and the TEMP DLL's sediment-interaction parameters); the Water Quality Analysis window's hydraulics-plan/profile/time-window pairing (wq.analysis.*); Water Quality Simulation Options (wq.sim_options.* - hydrodynamic continuity error resolution method, ULTIMATE limiter toggle, and maximum allowable computational time step, the latter operating alongside the model's dynamically-computed Courant/Peclet-constrained time step); and Output Options (wq.output.* - output timing mode and its interval/timestep value, the consolidated additional-output-variable selection checklist, daily max/min/mean/range output toggle, restart-file write toggle and write time, detailed log output toggle, temperature-override toggle and value, and per-constituent reference values for plotting). Explicitly excluded per scope (results-viewing/display-only, one-time actions, or not-yet-implemented features, consistent with this catalog's existing exclusion precedents): the WQ Spatial Plot and Time Series Plot viewers and their color-scale/legend/animation controls, the 'Show Table of WQ Cells' and 'Show cell Interpolated values' read-only review tables, the boundary-condition 'Plot only selected Data Source vs Plot all defined Data Sources' display toggle (a display-only choice that does not change what is simulated), the 'Show Temperature Correction Columns' column-visibility checkbox, the Computations Log File viewer itself (as opposed to the Detailed Log Output toggle that controls whether it is written, which IS catalogued), and per-project DSS/Excel file linkage mechanics beyond what is captured in the consolidated four-source time-series pattern. Also explicitly excluded because the manual states outright they are not yet implemented in this version of HEC-RAS, rather than guessed at: Water Quality Regions (§3.4 - would allow spatially-varying WQ parameter sets, but the manual's own "Not Yet Implemented" notice says setting/editing/managing them is not yet available) and per-cell (as opposed to systemwide) assignment of Water Quality Parameters (§8.3.4 - the manual states this version applies WQ parameters systemwide only). Also excluded as one-time actions or file-management mechanics rather than persisted model-data fields, consistent with the existing DSS-import and save-action exclusion precedents: Managing Water Quality Data Files (§8.2 - save/rename/delete of the WQ dataset file itself, analogous to project-file management elsewhere in HEC-RAS), the Preparing WQ Input requirement checklists (§8.5.1 - informational lists of what data must exist elsewhere, not new dialog fields), Running the Water Quality Model / the Compute button and its status window (§7.2, §8.5.2), and the Zero-Dimension (CSTR) model (§6.4.1) - a testing/experimentation mode that reuses the same wq.library.*/wq.constituent.* parameters already catalogued rather than exposing distinct fields of its own, and requires no geometry, hydraulics, or hydrodynamics file. Flagged for live HEC-RAS 7.0 confirmation rather than guessed, because the manual names or implies these fields but does not give field-level control_type/valid_range detail: the GCSM maximum-constituent-count field (manual renders it as an unfilled 'up to ___' blank placeholder); the NSMII sediment-diagenesis submodel's full per-parameter dialog (pore-water diffusion/particle-mixing coefficients and sediment PON/POP/POC diagenesis rates have temperature-correction defaults tabulated in §12.3 but no other range/default table); the NSMII state-variable count/list itself, where the manual internally conflicts between "up to 16" (§5.3.1/§8.7.2, matching the 16 variables enumerated in §13.7) and "twenty four" (§1 introduction, describing a fuller NSM including sediment diagenesis); the KLEIN solar-radiation module's Precipitable Water Content and Cloud Cover parameters and all four MBH module parameters (named but not given numeric ranges/defaults, unlike the Dust Coefficient which is documented separately in §11.8.1); the TEMP DLL's three sediment-interaction parameters (Sediment Layer Thickness, Sediment Bulk Density, Sediment Specific Heat - each exists only as an unfilled subsection heading in the manual with no body text); the wind anemometer non-standard-height correction's surface-characterization dropdown option labels; the WQ output time-interval dropdown's enumerated value list (parallel to the existing flagged gap for unsteady hydrograph Data-time-interval values); and the observed-data Applicable Duration dropdown's enumerated option list; the Solids Simulation Library (SOLIDS DLL) - the manual documents only its activation checkbox (within wq.library.active_libraries, §5.4.1/§8.7.4/§13.3) and gives zero field-level detail anywhere in the document on its own parameters (e.g. settling velocity, resuspension rate) despite SOLIDS being one of the four selectable library groups, so no SOLIDS-specific parameter fields were added rather than invented; and the TEQ (Equilibrium Temperature) DLL's own parameter dialog - the manual describes only the governing equilibrium-temperature equation (§13.5, referencing an equilibrium temperature Te and an overall heat exchange coefficient K) with no field-level description of an input dialog analogous to TEMP's Parameters tab, so TEQ's specific input fields (beyond its activation checkbox in wq.library.active_libraries) were not catalogued. Water Quality module is now considered fully catalogued against this manual. fields.valid_range_units: same format as upstream Flow Series; enters model downstream of the specified XS

fields.dialog_path: Quasi-Unsteady Flow Editor > Add Flow Change Location(s) > Uniform Lateral Flow
fields.valid_range_units: distributed by reach-length-weighted average; cannot span junctions, bridges, inline/lateral structures

fields.dialog_path: Quasi-Unsteady Flow Editor > T.S. Gate Openings
fields.field_name: Time Series Gate Openings (per gate group)
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m opening; required for every gate group if an inline structure has gates, even if unused
fields.notes: Manual advises against quasi-unsteady gate operation for most applications (does not conserve mass / route through reservoirs).

fields.dialog_path: Quasi-Unsteady Flow Editor > Internal Stage BC
fields.field_name: Internal Stage Boundary Condition (reservoir stage control)
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m; blank entries revert that time step to a backwater computation (e.g. to simulate gate-controlled flush periods)

fields.dialog_path: Quasi-Unsteady Flow Editor > Set Temperature
fields.valid_range_units: deg F or deg C; single value per time step for the whole model
fields.notes: Required input for fall velocity / viscosity computations; program does not supply a default if omitted (unlike unsteady mode).

fields.dialog_path: Unsteady Flow Data Editor > Options > Water Temperature (for Unsteady Sediment)
fields.valid_range_units: deg F or deg C; can be entered at Data Time Interval as coarse as 1 Month
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D field. Defaults to 55.4°F if left unspecified.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Transport Function
fields.valid_range_units: 1D: Ackers-White | Engelund-Hansen | Laursen-Copeland | Meyer-Peter Müller | Toffaleti | MPM-Toffaleti | Yang | Wilcock-Crowe (8 options). 2D adds: Soulsby-van Rijn | van Rijn | Wu (11 options total).
fields.notes: Single global setting per sediment file; results highly sensitive to selection per manual warnings.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Sorting Method
fields.valid_range_units: Thomas (Ex5) | Copeland (Ex7) | Active Layer
fields.notes: 1D only per 2DSED-6.4.1 §3.1.2, p.34 - the dropdown is visible but inert for 2D, which always uses an active-layer-like approach with arbitrary layer count.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Fall Velocity Method
fields.valid_range_units: Rubey | Toffaleti | Van Rijn | Dietrich | Report 12 (1D); 2D adds Soulsby | Wu and Wang
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D field/dialog.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters (per cross section)
fields.field_name: Max Depth or Min Elevation (sediment control-volume vertical extent)
fields.valid_range_units: Max Depth: ft/m below original invert; Min Elev: ft/m hard elevation; entering one clears the other
fields.notes: Required (with Movable Bed Limits) for every cross section for the model to run.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Sta Left / Sta Right (per cross section)
fields.control_type: numeric input pair, per cross section
fields.valid_range_units: cross-section station; inclusive of the node at that station
fields.notes: Also scales unit-width transport capacity for several transport functions; the Use Banks for Extents tool is a one-time populate action, not a separate field.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Number of Mobile Bed Channels
fields.field_name: Number of Mobile Bed Channels (Multiple Movable Bed Limits)
fields.valid_range_units: 1 or more; expands the movable-bed-limit table to one Sta Left/Sta Right pair per channel, per cross section
fields.notes: Used for flow splits/braided channels and reservoir deltas with multiple active sub-channels.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Initial Conditions and Transport Parameters > Bed Gradation column (per cross section)
fields.field_name: Bed Gradation Template Assignment (per cross section)
fields.data_type: enum (template name, or blank to interpolate)
fields.valid_range_units: selects from user-defined Bed Gradation Templates
fields.notes: Cross sections left blank between two defined templates are auto-interpolated and marked 'Interpolated' - this marker is a derived display state, not independently editable data.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Define/Edit Bed Gradation
fields.control_type: table + radio buttons + New Bed Gradation Sample button
fields.data_type: array of {grain_class, value} plus format flag
fields.valid_range_units: either % Finer (cumulative, by upper-bound diameter) or Grain Class Fraction/Weight (per class, normalized); 20 grain classes
fields.source: 1DSED-6.4.1 §1.2.1.6.1, p.70-71; also usable via Multiple Bed Gradation Table bulk-entry grid, p.74-75
fields.notes: Database entity referenced by cross sections (1D), 2D bed material classifications, and BSTEM material gradation.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Define/Edit Bed Gradation > Set Sample Specific Cohesive Parameters
fields.data_type: bool + float x4 (tau_c, M, tau_c_MW, M_MW)
fields.valid_range_units: overrides the global Cohesive Options thresholds for cross sections/layers using this specific gradation template
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D concept; stored 'dormant' (retained but unused) if the checkbox is later unchecked.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Mixing Options > Specify Separate Cover/Active Layer Gradations
fields.field_name: Separate Cover/Active Layer Gradation + Initial Layer Thickness (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: initializes the cover layer (Thomas/Copeland) or active layer (Active Layer method); blank XS default to the main homogeneous gradation

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Add Sediment Boundary Location(s)
fields.control_type: table (auto-listed external boundaries + Add for internal)
fields.valid_range_units: external boundaries mandatory; internal locations optional, added via river-station selector

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Rating Curve
fields.field_name: Sediment Rating Curve (Flow-Load or Flow-Concentration pairs, with per-class gradation)
fields.valid_range_units: tons/day load or mg/L concentration; up to ~20 flow-load points; gradations as incremental (not cumulative) fractions/percentages per point
fields.notes: No extrapolation above the max entered flow (holds the largest load); log-interpolates below the min entered flow to zero at zero flow.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Rating Curve > Load/Concentration radio button
fields.field_name: Rating Curve Units Mode (Load vs Concentration)
fields.valid_range_units: Load (tons/day) | Concentration (mg/L); a Load<->Conc button converts entered values between modes

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Rating Curve > Define Diversion Load
fields.field_name: Diversion Load (negative-flow rating curve + per-grain-class diversion coefficients)
fields.valid_range_units: grain class coefficients 0-1 (fraction of computed mass diverted); restricted to lateral flow series boundaries
fields.notes: Manual recommends modeling diversions with Lateral Structures directly instead in most cases.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Sediment Load Series (Manual Entry)
fields.field_name: Sediment Load Series - Manual Entry (duration, load, gradation)
fields.valid_range_units: tons per time increment; negative loads allowed (simplified deposition/dredging) but should not mix sign within one series
fields.notes: Decoupled from any flow boundary; introduces sediment regardless of flow.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Sediment Load Series > DSS tab
fields.field_name: Sediment Load Series - DSS (per grain class DSS path)
fields.control_type: DSS path chooser, one path per grain class
fields.valid_range_units: DSS record C-part must equal 'Sediment'; data assumed Period-Cumulative (PER-CUM)
fields.notes: A Sediment Load Series can mix Manual Entry and DSS grain classes.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions (upstream boundary selection)
fields.valid_range_units: upstream boundaries only; computes boundary load = local transport capacity each time step

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions (boundary selection)
fields.valid_range_units: zero sediment load/concentration; HEC-RAS 6.0+

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Sediment Boundary Conditions > Define Sediment Split at Junction
fields.field_name: Sediment Split Method at Flow-Split Junctions
fields.valid_range_units: Flow Weighted (default) | Potential Weighted | Flow Weighted with Grain Class Threshold | Sediment Splits by Grain Class (per-class diverted-mass multipliers 0-1)
fields.notes: Only available/required at junctions with downstream flow splits; dendritic-only models cannot use this.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Define Grain Classes and Sediment Properties (User Defined Grain Classes)
fields.field_name: Grain Class Definitions (bounds, name, Specific Gravity/Porosity/Bulk Density)
fields.data_type: array of {min_mm, max_mm, name, SG, porosity, bulk_density}
fields.valid_range_units: defaults to AGU log-base-2 scale 0.002-2048mm across 20 classes; program requires exactly 20 grain classes though only classes present in bed/BCs are computed
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D dialog. First five grain classes are treated as cohesive regardless of edited size (see sed.cohesive.*).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Define Grain Classes > Enforce Adjacent-Non-Overlapping Grain Classes and Geometric Mean
fields.field_name: Enforce Adjacent-Non-Overlapping Grain Classes and Geometric Mean
fields.valid_range_units: default on; unchecking allows duplicate/overlapping grain classes and disables automatic geometric-mean computation
fields.notes: Manual warns that violating adjacency/ordering can corrupt Thomas/Copeland mixing algorithms.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Define Grain Classes and Sediment Properties > Specific Gravity
fields.valid_range_units: unitless; default 2.65
fields.notes: 1D applies one SG to the whole model; 2D allows per-grain-class SG as part of its variable-density algorithms (see sed.grainclass.definitions).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Method
fields.valid_range_units: Standard Transport Functions (default, not recommended) | Krone-Partheniades (HEC-RAS method) | Krone-Partheniades (HEC 6T method)
fields.notes: Applies to the first five grain classes (or user-redefined cohesive classes).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Erodibility Parameter Type
fields.field_name: Erodibility Parameter Type (Kd dimensional vs M dimensionless)
fields.valid_range_units: Kd (dimensional, Mass/Force-time) | M (dimensionless form)
fields.notes: Changes the units/interpretation of sed.cohesive.thresholds; shared 1D/2D concept.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options (global) or Bed Gradation > Sample Specific Cohesive Parameters
fields.field_name: Cohesive Erosion Thresholds/Rates (critical shear, erosion rate, mass-wasting threshold, mass-wasting rate)
fields.valid_range_units: critical shear stress ~0.2-0.8 Pa typical; erosion rate M ~0.01-50 Pa/hr typical (site-specific, spans orders of magnitude)
fields.notes: Global default plus optional per-gradation-sample override (sed.gradation.sample_specific_cohesive_params).

fields.dialog_path: 2D Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Flocculation
fields.valid_range_units: Hwang (1989) 4-coefficient method | User-Specified Flocculation Curve
fields.notes: 2D only.

fields.dialog_path: 2D Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Flocculation > Hwang (1989)
fields.valid_range_units: empirical coefficients; example literature values tabulated in manual range ~0.04-0.19 (first coefficient) and ~3.5-25 (second)
fields.notes: 2D only; corrected internally for water temperature relative to a 55.4°F reference.

fields.dialog_path: 2D Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Flocculation > User-Specified Curve
fields.field_name: User-Specified Flocculation Curve (settling velocity vs concentration)
fields.valid_range_units: settling velocity ft/s or m/s vs suspended sediment concentration mg/L
fields.notes: 2D only.

fields.dialog_path: 2D Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Cohesive Options > Consolidation
fields.field_name: Consolidation Curve (dry bulk density vs time)
fields.valid_range_units: one global curve for the entire model domain
fields.notes: 2D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options (Global Bed Change Editor)
fields.field_name: Global Bed Change Method (2x2 matrix: Channel/Overbank x Erosion/Deposition)
fields.valid_range_units: default = Veneer (channel erosion+deposition, overbank deposition only, no overbank erosion); channel/overbank boundary defined by Movable Bed Limits, not bank stations
fields.notes: 1D only. Channel erosion and deposition are mandatory; overbank erosion/deposition are optional toggles.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options (Overbank/Channel Deposition dropdown)
fields.valid_range_units: Veneer | Reservoir (depth-dependent) | Distance-Decay Floodplain | Rouse-Diffusion
fields.notes: 1D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options > Rouse-Diffusion Coefficients
fields.valid_range_units: Beta: floodplain deposition inversely related, <1 puts more sediment in overbank; DT: 0=spread evenly, 1=concentrate near channel (levee-forming)
fields.notes: 1D only. Requires movable bed limits at or inside bank stations.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options (Channel Erosion dropdown)
fields.valid_range_units: Veneer | Simplified CEM (Channel Evolution Model)
fields.notes: 1D only; CEM is applied only to cross sections that also have Max Width/Side Slope data (sed.bedchange.cem_params).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options > Simplified CEM parameters (per cross section)
fields.field_name: Simplified CEM Parameters (Max Width, Side Slope, Center Station)
fields.valid_range_units: Max Width ft/m; Side Slope H:V; Center Station (optional) is a cross-section station
fields.notes: 1D only; Adkinson (1996) regression Width Calculator button computes a starting estimate.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options > XS Specific Bed Change Options
fields.data_type: array of {xs, channel_erosion, channel_deposition, overbank_erosion, overbank_deposition}
fields.valid_range_units: overrides the global 2x2 matrix for the listed cross sections
fields.notes: 1D only; manual warns this should apply to morphologically coherent reaches, not individual cross sections.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Change Options > Area-Volume Conversion Method
fields.valid_range_units: Backwards Compatible | Average End Area (HEC-6) | Simpson | Single-V (rectangle)
fields.notes: 1D only; controls both bed-sorting and bed-change area/volume math.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Sediment Routing Method
fields.field_name: Sediment Routing Method (Limit to Water Velocity)
fields.valid_range_units: Standard (unlimited sediment velocity) | Limit to Water Velocity
fields.notes: 1D only; manual recommends Limit to Water Velocity for reservoirs/low-velocity depositional zones.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Transport Function Calibration and Modification > Modify Transport Functions checkbox
fields.field_name: Modify Transport Functions with Factors or Parameters (master enable)
fields.valid_range_units: if unchecked, edited calibration values are stored but not used in computations
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D concept, though the 2D editor is a separate dialog (see sed.2d.calibration.*).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Transport Function Calibration and Modification > Scaling Factors
fields.field_name: Transport Function Scaling Factor + Critical Mobility Scaling Factor (per function)
fields.valid_range_units: linear multipliers on capacity and critical mobility respectively; not all functions expose a mobility factor (e.g. Engelund-Hansen, Toffaleti)
fields.notes: Preferred (since v5.1) calibration method over direct parameter overrides.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Transport Function Calibration and Modification > Define Transport Function Parameters and Coefficients
fields.valid_range_units: exposes critical shear/threshold-mobility/reference-shear plus coefficient and exponent for four functions (Laursen-Copeland, MPM, Ackers-White, Wilcock)
fields.notes: Not recommended (manual prefers scaling factors); includes a Use Wong and Parker Correction to MPM button that auto-populates a=4.93, critical Shields=0.047, exponent=1.6, form-drag=1.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Transport Function Calibration and Modification > Toffaleti Limiter
fields.valid_range_units: limits suspended-zone transport to grain classes below a shear-velocity/fall-velocity ratio threshold
fields.notes: Addresses a documented Toffaleti/MPM-Toffaleti discontinuity in high-energy conditions.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Lateral Weir Options
fields.field_name: Lateral Structure Sediment Diversion Threshold (grain class screen, per structure)
fields.valid_range_units: diverts flow-weighted percentage of sediment finer than or equal to the selected grain class only; coarser classes excluded
fields.notes: Default assumption without this option is full flow-weighted diversion of all grain classes.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Flow Optimization > Lateral Structures/Diversions tab
fields.field_name: Lateral Structures/Diversions Flow Optimization (iterative feedback for quasi-unsteady)
fields.valid_range_units: not default; increases run time substantially due to per-time-step iteration
fields.notes: Only relevant to quasi-unsteady models, since unsteady flow accounts for these feedbacks implicitly.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Mixing Options > Shape Factor
fields.valid_range_units: unitless, 0-1 (1=spherical); only used by the Report 12 fall velocity method

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Mixing Options > Active Layer Thickness
fields.valid_range_units: 1*d90 (default) | X*d90 with user Multiplier (typically 1-5 for gravel beds, >10-100 for sand beds)
fields.notes: Only affects the Active Layer sorting method, not Thomas/Copeland.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Bed Mixing Options > Min Thickness
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m; guards against active layer exhaustion when the d90-based thickness becomes very small

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Subsidence (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m per unit time; constant rate, applied to all nodes (inside and outside movable bed limits) over the simulation duration

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Pass Through Nodes
fields.field_name: Classic Pass Through Nodes (cross section list)
fields.valid_range_units: selected cross sections have capacity forced equal to supply (no erosion/deposition)
fields.notes: Does not prevent BSTEM bank failure/toe scour, only vertical bed change.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Set Pass Through Nodes > Pool
fields.field_name: Pool Pass Through Nodes (cross section list)
fields.valid_range_units: adopts the transport capacity of a bounding, non-pass-through cross section instead of a fixed no-change assumption

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Transport Methods > 1D Methods (Pool Pass Through capacity method)
fields.valid_range_units: Upstream Capacity | US and Lagged DS (averages upstream same-time-step and downstream previous-time-step capacity)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > Observed Data > Profile
fields.valid_range_units: can tag a standard HEC-RAS sediment output variable (shows with _obs suffix) or a fully custom variable name; blank date/time makes the profile persistent across all time steps
fields.notes: Mirrors the existing precedent of unsteady.observed.* entries - persisted calibration data stored in the sediment file.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: inflection point between bank and top-of-bank; left half of the cross section (relative to thalweg)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: analogous to Left Bank Edge Station, right half of the cross section

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: can be auto-set via Set Toe Station to Bank Stations / to Movable Bed Stations buttons

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: analogous to Left Bank Toe Station

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > GW Elev (per bank, per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m; static value if Static groundwater option selected, or initial elevation if Dynamic
fields.notes: Results very sensitive to this parameter; no physical floor on negative pore pressure in current version.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab (per bank)
fields.valid_range_units: Static (fixed GW elevation) | Dynamic (routed via hydraulic conductivity/reservoir length, see sed.bstem.material_groundwater_params)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > Left/Right Bank Material (per cross section)
fields.valid_range_units: 16 pre-defined default USDA-ARS material types | user-defined custom material | Define Layers (multi-layer)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > Define/Edit BSTEM Sample Parameters
fields.field_name: BSTEM Material Soil Strength Parameters (Unit Weight, Friction Angle, Cohesion, Phi-b, Gradation Sample)
fields.valid_range_units: saturated unit weight lb/ft3 or kg/m3; friction angle degrees; cohesion psf/kPa; phi-b typically 10-30 degrees, maxes at friction angle when saturated

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > Define/Edit BSTEM Sample Parameters (erodibility)
fields.field_name: BSTEM Material Erodibility Parameters (Critical Shear Stress, Erodibility)
fields.valid_range_units: critical shear stress and erodibility rate (units per selected erodibility parameter type); Simon et al. (2000) regression available as a fallback when unmeasured

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > Define/Edit BSTEM Sample Parameters (groundwater, optional)
fields.field_name: BSTEM Material Groundwater Parameters (Hydraulic Conductivity, Reservoir Length)
fields.valid_range_units: only used if Dynamic groundwater option selected; Darcy K and bank-reservoir length (perpendicular to river)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > USDA-ARS BSTEM tab > Define Layers (per cross section/bank)
fields.field_name: BSTEM Bank Material Layers (bottom elevation + material, multi-layer)
fields.valid_range_units: bottom elevations must be entered low to high; deepest layer must extend to/below the thalweg

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > USDA-ARS BSTEM Options
fields.field_name: Number of Failure Plane Computation Nodes
fields.valid_range_units: default 100 (evenly spaced between bank toe and edge elevations)

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > USDA-ARS BSTEM Options
fields.field_name: Number of Time Steps Between Failure Computations
fields.valid_range_units: skips bank failure computations to reduce run time; trades off accuracy since FS<1 conditions typically persist several time steps

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > USDA-ARS BSTEM Options > Grain Shear Correction
fields.valid_range_units: Strickler (default) | None
fields.notes: Turning off increases shear on the bank and increases scour.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > USDA-ARS BSTEM Options > Min % Cohesive
fields.field_name: Minimum Percent Cohesive to Use Toe Scour (Cohesive) Algorithms
fields.valid_range_units: default 20%; determines whether toe scour uses cohesive excess-shear equations or cohesionless transport functions per soil layer

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > BSTEM Options > Transport Function
fields.valid_range_units: Engelund-Hansen | Parker (1990) | Wilcock and Crowe (2000) | Meyer-Peter Müller | Wu (2000)
fields.notes: Used only for soil layers below the cohesive threshold (sed.bstem.options.min_pct_cohesive_toe_scour).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Data Editor > Options > BSTEM Options > Toe Scour Mixing Method
fields.valid_range_units: Cumulative | Maximum Prevalence (default) | Maximum Capacity

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Simulation Time Window
fields.field_name: Simulation Time Window (start/end date and time)
fields.data_type: string x4 (start date, start time, end date, end time)
fields.valid_range_units: DDMMMYYYY date format, 2400-clock time
fields.notes: Applies to quasi-unsteady Sediment Transport Analysis window; unsteady sediment plans use the Unsteady Flow Analysis window's equivalent field.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.field_name: Bed Exchange Iterations / Bed Mixing Time Steps (SPI)
fields.valid_range_units: default 10; recommended range 1-50
fields.notes: 1D quasi-unsteady/unsteady sediment computational tolerance.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.field_name: Minimum Bed Change Before Updating Hydraulics
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m; defaults to same value as sed.plan.min_bed_change_update_xs but independently editable
fields.notes: Manual describes this as a legacy feature that can introduce instability; recommends testing sensitivity or setting to 0.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.field_name: Minimum Bed Change Before Updating Cross Sections
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m; default 0.02 ft

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.valid_range_units: selected by default; not applied to cross sections using BSTEM

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.valid_range_units: Local Energy Slope (default) | Average Energy Slope - Cell Centered | Average Energy Slope - Downwind
fields.notes: Only affects sediment transport equations, not hydraulic results; Average methods recommended for headcuts/dam removals.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.valid_range_units: None | Limerinos | Brownlie | Van Rijn
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D field/dialog (1D allows sub-reach definition via sed.plan.bed_roughness_averaging_reaches; 2D applies to all wet cells).

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances > Select Reach to Average Bed Roughness Predictors
fields.field_name: Bed Roughness Averaging Reaches (grouped cross-section ranges)
fields.valid_range_units: averages hydraulic/sediment parameters over the grouped cross sections to smooth a single predicted roughness
fields.notes: 1D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis / Unsteady Flow Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances (General)
fields.valid_range_units: number of hydraulic time steps per sediment computation increment (unsteady only); default 1; recommended <10
fields.notes: Shared 1D/2D concept (2D manual calls it 'Sediment Computation Multiplier').

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Sediment Computation Options and Tolerances > Show XS Weights
fields.field_name: Cross Section Weighting Factors (hydraulic averaging for transport capacity)
fields.valid_range_units: default 0.25 (upstream) - 0.5 (computational) - 0.25 (downstream); can be spread over multiple XS or set to 0-1-0
fields.notes: 1D only; manual recommends 0-1-0 (i.e. disabled) for simplified/rectangular cross sections to avoid 'saw tooth' instability.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Dredging Events Editor
fields.field_name: Dredging Event (start time, end time, method)
fields.valid_range_units: 7 methods: 3 Elevation (Left-Right-Elev, Center-Width-Elev, Width-Elev) + 4 Mass (Left-Right-Mass Prism/Veneer, Width-Mass Prism/Veneer); default instantaneous removal at start time unless an end date is also given
fields.notes: 1D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Dredging Events Editor (Elevation method parameters)
fields.field_name: Dredge Elevation Method Parameters (Left/Right Sta or Center Sta/Width, + Elevation)
fields.valid_range_units: ft/m stations and elevation defining a rectangular dredge template
fields.notes: 1D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Dredging Events Editor (Mass method parameters)
fields.field_name: Dredge Mass Method Parameters (Left/Right Sta or Width, + Mass)
fields.valid_range_units: mass in tons; program computes the resulting geometry (Prism) or applies the veneer rule (Veneer)
fields.notes: 1D only.

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Dredging Events Editor > Set Values
fields.field_name: Set Range of Values (project non-uniform dredge elevations along a slope)
fields.valid_range_units: projects varying dredge elevations upstream/downstream instead of a constant value

fields.dialog_path: Sediment Transport Analysis window > Options > Dredging Events Editor > Re-Introduce Part of Dredged Load

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Cloudiness
fields.control_type: table / DSS chooser / Excel reference / constant / computed-from-observed-radiation
fields.data_type: array of {datetime, value} | float | string (DSS path) | string (Excel ref)
fields.valid_range_units: fraction of sky covered, 0-0.9 (0.1 clear, 0.5-0.9 broken, 0.9 overcast per manual guideline table)
fields.notes: Required for both calculated solar radiation and downwelling longwave radiation. May alternatively be computed from an observed shortwave-radiation time series rather than entered directly.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Solar Radiation
fields.control_type: table / DSS chooser / Excel reference / constant, or computed from lat/long+cloudiness+dust
fields.data_type: array of {datetime, value} | float | string (DSS path) | string (Excel ref)
fields.valid_range_units: units: W/m2, cal/cm2/day, or MJ/m2/day; internal calculations in W/m2
fields.notes: Primary driver for the water temperature model; if not measured directly, computed via wq.met.latitude_longitude, wq.weather.cloudiness_series, and wq.weather.solar_radiation_dust_coefficient using the selected Solar Radiation Module (wq.library.solar_radiation_module_select).

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Solar Radiation > Dust Coefficient
fields.valid_range_units: 0-0.2 (larger = more atmospheric attenuation by dust/scattering; urban areas tend toward 0.2, rural toward 0)
fields.notes: Often used as a calibration parameter for synthetic solar radiation. Also functions as the KLEIN solar-radiation-module's 'Dust Coefficient' adjustable parameter (§13.8).

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Wind Speed
fields.control_type: table / DSS chooser / Excel reference / constant
fields.data_type: array of {datetime, value} | float | string (DSS path) | string (Excel ref)
fields.valid_range_units: units: m/s, mph, or ft/s; internal calculations in m/s
fields.notes: Required for surface-flux (latent/sensible heat) estimation in the TEMP model.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Wind Speed > Non-Standard Height
fields.valid_range_units: standard anemometer height assumed = 2 m; if non-standard, enter actual elevation (m/ft) and select a surface-characterization option; raw data is corrected for height and surface roughness
fields.notes: Manual does not enumerate the specific surface-characterization dropdown option labels - flagged for live HEC-RAS 7.0 confirmation rather than guessed.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Wind Speed > Wind Function Parameters
fields.valid_range_units: a: calibration coefficient, order of 10^-6; b: calibration coefficient, order of 10^-6; c: coefficient, order of one

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Wind Speed > Wind Function Parameters
fields.valid_range_units: software allows 0.5-1.5; generally set to 1.0 (unity); recommended range 0.9-1.1
fields.notes: Partitions surface-flux energy between latent and sensible heat in the TEMP wind function.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Meteorologic Datasets > [station] > Wind Speed > Use Richardson number...
fields.valid_range_units: on/off; if off, the stability multiplier R in the wind function is fixed at 1
fields.notes: When on, adjusts surface-flux estimates for atmospheric stability (a function of air temp, water temp, and wind speed).

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Boundary Conditions > [location]
fields.field_name: Water Quality Boundary Condition (per constituent, per required location)
fields.control_type: table / DSS chooser / Excel reference / constant, with units dropdown
fields.data_type: array of {datetime, value} | float | string (DSS path) | string (Excel ref)
fields.valid_range_units: units depend on constituent (e.g. deg C/F for temperature, mg/L for nutrients); required at every location a flow boundary exists (upstream, downstream, tributary/lateral inflow, tidal boundary)
fields.notes: Required boundary locations are driven by the hydraulic model's flow boundaries; up to 4 data sources may be entered simultaneously per location, with the Data Source pulldown selecting which is actually used at run time. If a flow boundary is later removed from the hydraulics model, existing WQ boundary data becomes 'unattached' (still saved, but unused) - a status indicator, not a distinct field.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Initial Conditions > Add RS location(s) to the table...
fields.field_name: Initial Condition Distribution (per constituent, per river station)
fields.valid_range_units: units depend on constituent; at least one value required per constituent per reach; interpolated to all WQ computational points

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Initial Conditions
fields.field_name: Initial Conditions Source (Restart File vs Distribution)
fields.valid_range_units: Restart File | Initial Condition Distribution

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Initial Conditions > Restart File (file open icon)
fields.valid_range_units: *.wqrst files
fields.notes: Restart files are written by a separate run's Water Quality Computation Options (see wq.output.restart_write_toggle); default name is the writing plan's name + '.wqrst'.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Observed Data > [location/state variable]
fields.control_type: table / DSS chooser / Excel reference / constant
fields.data_type: array of {datetime, value} | float | string (DSS path) | string (Excel ref)

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Observed Data > [dataset] > Type
fields.valid_range_units: Continuous record | Grab sample

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Observed Data > [dataset] > Applicable Duration
fields.valid_range_units: manual does not enumerate specific duration options - flagged for live HEC-RAS 7.0 confirmation
fields.notes: Controls how long each grab-sample point is displayed on the WQ spatial data plot; a display-window parameter, not a hydraulic/kinetic one.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Observed Data > [dataset] > Downstream distance from RS to gage
fields.field_name: Downstream Distance from RS to Gage

Water Quality Model Configuration window > GCSM > Parameters tab

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Model Configuration window > GCSM > Parameters tab (Temperature Correction column)
fields.valid_range_units: typically 1.01-1.10; suggested default 1.047 for GCSM zero/first-order and sediment-release rates per manual's default-value table
fields.notes: Used in the Modified Arrhenius temperature-correction equation applied to each rate; entered per rate constant, per constituent.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Mass Injection > Add RS location(s) to the Table...
fields.valid_range_units: mass units consistent with the constituent; injected instantaneously into the WQ cell just downstream of the selected river station, during the WQ time step bounding the injection time

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Data Editor > Edit... > Water Quality Model Configuration window > Available Libraries tab
fields.valid_range_units: General Constituent Simulation Library (GCSM) | Nutrient Simulation Library (NSMII) | Solids Simulation Library (SOLIDS) | Water Temperature - Full Energy Budget (TEMP) | Water Temperature - Equilibrium (TEQ); one or more may be activated together; water temperature may alternatively be held constant (no temperature DLL active)

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Model Configuration window > NSMII > State Variables list
fields.field_name: NSMII State Variable Enable (Yes/No per variable)
fields.valid_range_units: manual's Nutrient Simulation Library overview (§5.3.1, §8.7.2) states 'up to 16' selectable state variables (matching the 16 enumerated in §13.7: NH4, NO3, OrgN, PO4/inorganic P, OrgP, particulate organic C, DOX, algae, benthic algae, dissolved organic C, dissolved inorganic C, dissolved N2, alkalinity, pathogen, CBOD, suspended solids); the manual's introduction (§1) separately describes NSM as having 'twenty four water quality state variables' including a full sediment-diagenesis submodel - flagged as an internal manual inconsistency needing live-7.0 confirmation of the exact selectable list and count

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Model Configuration window > NSMII > Nutrient Parameter window (top pulldown)
fields.valid_range_units: Liebig's Limiting Nutrient formulation | Multiplicative formulation

fields.data_type: array of {symbol, description, units, suggested_range, default, temp_correction}
fields.valid_range_units: alpha0 (Chla:algae ratio) 10-100 ug Chla/mgA, default 10; mu_max (max algal growth) 1.0-3.0 day^-1, default 1.0, theta=1.047; rho (algal respiration) 0.05-0.5 day^-1, default 0.05, theta=1.047; KL (light half-saturation) 4-20 W/m2, default 4; KN (N half-saturation) 0.01-0.30 mgN/L, default 0.01; KP (P half-saturation) 0.001-0.05 mgP/L, default 0.001; lambda0 (non-algal light extinction) default 0.03 m^-1; lambda1 (linear self-shading) 0.007-0.07, default 0.007; lambda2 (non-linear self-shading) variable, default 0.05; sigma1 (algal settling rate) 0.1-2.0 m/day, default 0.1, theta=1.024
fields.notes: Suggested ranges and defaults sourced from Brown and Barnwell (1987), QUAL2E. Defaults are generally set to the lowest value in the suggested range.

fields.data_type: array of {symbol, description, units, suggested_range, default, temp_correction}

fields.data_type: array of {symbol, description, units, suggested_range, default, temp_correction}

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Model Configuration window > TEMP/TEQ > Solar Radiation Module
fields.valid_range_units: EPA (no adjustable parameters, used by CE-QUAL-W2) | KLEIN (Precipitable Water Content, Dust Coefficient, Cloud Cover - used by QUAL2E/CE-QUAL-RIV1) | MBH (Ratio of Forward-Scattered Irradiance, Aerosol Absorptance Coefficient, Atmospheric Turbidity, Ozone Parameters - used by QUAL2kw)

fields.valid_range_units: any existing calibrated steady or unsteady flow plan for the project
fields.notes: Pairs a hydrodynamics plan with a Water Quality Input file to form the WQ simulation.

fields.valid_range_units: any profile defined in the associated steady flow plan
fields.notes: Required only if the associated hydraulics plan is from a steady flow analysis (unsteady-flow plans do not need this).

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Simulation Time Window
fields.valid_range_units: for an unsteady-flow-based plan, must not start before or extend beyond the associated unsteady flow analysis's own time window (need not match it exactly)

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > Resolution of Hydrodynamic Continuity Error
fields.valid_range_units: Preserve concentration (adds/subtracts volume to resolve hydrodynamic continuity error, at the cost of exact constituent mass conservation) | Conserve mass (conserves constituent mass but leaves the hydrodynamic continuity error uncorrected, which can produce irregular concentrations)
fields.notes: Addresses small volume-continuity mismatches between the hydraulics model's and the WQ model's independent continuity solutions.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > ULTIMATE Limiter
fields.valid_range_units: on/off
fields.notes: Universal flux limiter (Leonard 1991) for the QUICKEST advection scheme; suppresses non-physical oscillation/non-monotonicity in computed cell concentrations by substituting the cell-face solution when triggered.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > Maximum Allowable Time Step
fields.valid_range_units: hours (or finer); the WQ engine dynamically computes a time step each interval to satisfy Courant < 0.9 and Peclet < 0.4, then also caps it at this user value - the smallest of the three governs
fields.notes: Useful to force a coarser-than-otherwise-necessary time step (e.g. for a desired hourly water-temperature output cadence) even when Courant/Peclet constraints would otherwise allow a longer step.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > Output Options
fields.valid_range_units: Output on an even time interval (requires interpolation, since the WQ computational time step is not evenly spaced) | Output on a selected number of time steps (no interpolation)

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > Output Options > (selected number of time steps)

fields.notes: Active only when wq.output.interval_mode = 'selected number of time steps'.

fields.dialog_path: Water Quality Analysis window > Options > Simulation Options... > Additional Output Variables
